variants.label: set-and-sigma-algebra-pair
variants.text: A measurable space is a pair (X,Σ), where X is a set and Σ is a σ-algebra of subsets of X.

mathematical_review: ProofWiki explicitly defines a measurable space as a set equipped with a sigma-algebra. It does not require a measure, probability distribution or topological structure. The independently screened sigma-algebra meaning supplies an exact noncircular prerequisite; measure space is a further context with an additional measure map.

variants.label: normalized-measure-space
variants.text: A probability space is a triple (Ω,Σ,P) where (Ω,Σ) is a measurable space and P is a countably additive measure on Σ satisfying P(Ω)=1.

mathematical_review: ProofWiki defines a probability space as a measure space with total measure one. Probability measure countable additivity and nonnegativity are part of the measure definition; normalized total mass is a distinctive condition. This can be a target for stochastic-process and conditional-expectation meanings after independently screening the measurable-space and measure prerequisites. The empty space admits no probability measure with P(Ω)=1, so it is excluded by the axioms, not by an arbitrary extra clause.

domain: probability: measurable functions on probability spaces

variants.label: general-measurable-valued-variable
variants.text: Given a probability space (Ω,F,P) and a measurable space (S,SigmaS), a random variable with values in S is an (F,SigmaS)-measurable map X:Ω→S.

variants.label: real-valued-random-variable
variants.text: A real-valued random variable on (Ω,F,P) is an F/B(R)-measurable map X:Ω→R, where B(R) is the Borel σ-algebra; equivalently the preimage of every interval (−∞,a] belongs to F.

mathematical_review: The direct ProofWiki random-variable page separates the general measurable-space-valued and real-valued formulations. Real-valued measurability has an equivalent half-infinite-interval inverse-image criterion. These two variants have different codomain scopes; do not merge their object contexts silently or confuse a 'continuous random variable' with a continuous sample path. General random variable and real-valued random variable can be displayed in appropriate educational ordering and linked to probability/measurable spaces when independently screened.

domain: algebra: left/right actions of rings on abelian groups

variants.label: left-action
variants.text: A left module M over a ring R is an abelian group (M,+) together with a left scalar action R×M→M distributive in each argument and associative with ring multiplication.

variants.label: right-action
variants.text: A right module M over a ring R is an abelian group (M,+) with a right scalar action M×R→M satisfying the analogous distributivity and multiplication-compatibility axioms.

mathematical_review: ProofWiki explicitly distinguishes left and right module axioms, with possibly different conventions regarding rings and unit actions. Before admitting into the independently screened corpus, check whether the source assumes a multiplicative identity and whether 1_R·m=m is demanded, then label left/right and unital/nonunital contexts precisely. The earlier source-screened submodule meaning presupposes a left module, so source-convention mismatches must not be glossed over.
review_blocker: Require source-specific unit-axiom check or another precise module source before mathematical promotion.
